title: Growth rate of list Ramsey numbers (Alon–Buci\'c–Kalvari–Kuperwasser–Szab\'o)
statement_text: Which side of the bounds $e^{\sqrt{k}\log(\chi(H)-1)/(4r)} \leq R_\ell(H,k) \leq (1-\pi(H)+o(1))^{-km(H)}$ is closer to the truth for a fixed $r$-graph $H$ that is not $r$-partite?
context_text: Alon, Buci\'c, Kalvari, Kuperwasser, and Szab\'o introduced the list Ramsey number $R_\ell(H,k)$ and proved the sub-exponential lower bound and exponential upper bound above, then asked which side better reflects the true asymptotic growth. In stark contrast, no exponential upper bound is known for the classical Ramsey number $R(K_3,k)$.
attributed_to: Alon, Buci\'c, Kalvari, Kuperwasser, and Szab\'o
paper_contribution: Proves that $R_\ell(H,k) = e^{\Theta(k)}$ for every $r$-graph $H$ that is not $r$-partite, establishing that the exponential upper bound gives the correct order of growth and fully resolving the question.
paper_title: Multicolor list Ramsey numbers grow exponentially

title: Conjecture on $R_\ell(\mathcal{H}_s, k)$
statement_text: For $s \geq 2$, if $\mathcal{H}_s$ is the family of graphs with chromatic number greater than $s$, then $R_\ell(\mathcal{H}_s, k) = s^k + 1$.
context_text: For a list assignment $L:E(K_n)\to\binom{\mathbb{N}}{k}$ giving each edge of $K_n$ a set of $k$ colours, an $L$-colouring is an edge-colouring in which each edge $e$ receives a colour from $L(e)$. The $k$-colour list Ramsey number $R_\ell(H,k)$ (introduced by Alon, Bucić, Kalvari, Kuperwasser and Szabó) is the smallest $n$ such that there is some $L:E(K_n)\to\binom{\mathbb{N}}{k}$ for which every $L$-colouring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$; taking $L$ constant shows $R_\ell(H,k)\le R(H,k)$, the classical $k$-colour Ramsey number. (The paper works more generally with $r$-uniform hypergraphs.) For a family $\mathcal{H}$ of graphs, $R_\ell(\mathcal{H},k)$ is the minimum $n$ such that some $L:E(K_n)\to\binom{\mathbb{N}}{k}$ forces, in every $L$-colouring of $K_n$, a monochromatic copy of some $H\in\mathcal{H}$. The authors state (proof omitted) that for $s\ge2$ and $\mathcal{H}_s$ the family of graphs with chromatic number greater than $s$, $\frac{1}{e}\cdot s^k\le R_\ell(\mathcal{H}_s,k)\le s^k+1$: the lower bound comes from their random construction for single graphs, which avoids every graph of chromatic number at least $\chi(H)$, and the upper bound from $R_\ell(\mathcal{H}_s,k)\le R(\mathcal{H}_s,k)=s^k+1$. They conjecture that the upper bound is the truth, i.e. that for this family the list Ramsey number equals the classical one.
paper_title: Multicolor list Ramsey numbers grow exponentially

title: Determine the exponential constant in $R_\ell(H,k)$
statement_text: It would be interesting to determine $\lim_{k\to\infty} R_\ell(H,k)^{1/k}$, even in just the case $H = K_3$.
context_text: For a list assignment $L:E(K_n)\to\binom{\mathbb{N}}{k}$ giving each edge of $K_n$ a set of $k$ colours, an $L$-colouring is an edge-colouring in which each edge $e$ receives a colour from $L(e)$. The $k$-colour list Ramsey number $R_\ell(H,k)$ (introduced by Alon, Bucić, Kalvari, Kuperwasser and Szabó) is the smallest $n$ such that there is some $L:E(K_n)\to\binom{\mathbb{N}}{k}$ for which every $L$-colouring of $K_n$ contains a monochromatic copy of $H$; taking $L$ constant shows $R_\ell(H,k)\le R(H,k)$, the classical $k$-colour Ramsey number. (The paper works more generally with $r$-uniform hypergraphs.) Alon et al. proved that if $H$ is not bipartite, $e^{\sqrt{k\log(\chi(H)-1)/4}}\le R_\ell(H,k)\le(1-\pi(H)+o(1))^{-k\,m(H)}$, where $\pi(H)=\lim_n \mathrm{ex}(n,H)\binom{n}{2}^{-1}$ is the Turán density and $m(H)=\max_{H'\subseteq H,\,e(H')>1}\frac{e(H')-1}{v(H')-2}$. The authors prove the lower bound $R_\ell(H,k)\ge\frac{1}{e}(1-\pi(H))^{-k}$, so $R_\ell(H,k)$ is exponential in $k$ if and only if $H$ is not bipartite (and polynomial otherwise). Since $m(H)>1$ for non-bipartite $H$, the two exponential constants differ, and the results do not determine $\lim_{k\to\infty}R_\ell(H,k)^{1/k}$ or even show that it exists. For $H=K_3$ the bounds read $\frac{1}{e}\cdot2^k\le R_\ell(K_3,k)\le(4+o(1))^k$, whereas no exponential upper bound is known for the classical $R(K_3,k)$; showing $R_\ell(K_3,k)\le3.199^k$ would, by the best known lower bound for $R(K_3,k)$, give $R_\ell(K_3,k)<R(K_3,k)$.
